issues.title: orgId parameter not propagated in getTeamIdsWithPermission
issues.description: The method getTeamIdsWithPermission accepts an orgId parameter to scope permission checks to a specific organization, but it fails to pass this parameter to the underlying getTeamIdsWithPermissions method. This causes organization scoping to be ignored when checking single permissions, allowing users to potentially access teams from all organizations instead of only the specified one. The bug breaks the core security feature introduced in this PR where organization-scoped permission checks were meant to restrict access based on orgId.

issues.title: Incomplete orgId filtering in PBAC child team query
issues.description: In the SQL query for getTeamsWithPBACPermissions, the WHERE clause for child teams is missing a check for child."parentId" = ${orgId}. The original PR added this condition to properly scope child teams when an orgId is provided, but this implementation only checks org."id" and child."id", missing the case where a child team's parent should match the orgId. This causes the query to incorrectly exclude child teams whose parentId matches the specified orgId, breaking the inheritance model where organization permissions should propagate to child teams.

issues.title: Authorization bypass when filtering multiple userIds including current user
issues.description: The isCurrentUser check was changed from a strict equality check (filters.userIds.length === 1 && user.id === filters.userIds[0]) to a loose inclusion check (filters.userIds.includes(user.id)). This allows a user to bypass permission checks by including their own userId in a list alongside other userIds they don't have permission to access. For example, if a user requests bookings for [ownUserId, unauthorizedUserId], the check passes even though they lack permission for the unauthorized user, allowing them to access bookings they shouldn't see.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25434 - fix: get bookings handler for pbac and fallback roles
pr.author: tomerqodo

structured_output.summary:
The PR moves the bookings list handler (`getBookings` in `get.handler.ts`) off direct ADMIN/OWNER membership queries and onto `PermissionCheckService.getTeamIdsWithPermission("booking.read")`, so PBAC custom roles and fallback ADMIN/OWNER roles both grant booking visibility. It also threads an optional `orgId` through the service, the repository interface, and the SQL in `PermissionRepository`, intending to scope team results to the caller's organization.

The direction is right, but the change has two authorization defects. First, the single-permission repository method accepts `orgId` and then drops it before calling the plural method, so the org scope the handler asks for never reaches SQL. Users with ADMIN/OWNER or PBAC roles in other organizations would now see those members' bookings, which the old membership query had blocked. Second, the `isCurrentUser` check was loosened from "exactly one id equal to me" to "list contains me". A request with `userIds: [me, victim]` now passes the FORBIDDEN guard, and the booking query then returns the victim's bookings. The unit tests don't catch either problem: the one org-scoped test case uses a user with `orgId: null`, and the "own userId" assertions use `resolves.not.toThrow()`, which can't fail.

Verdict: request changes. Both critical items are small fixes, but they gate data exposure, so they should land before merge.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Two critical authorization defects: (1) the `orgId` scope is silently discarded in `PermissionRepository.getTeamIdsWithPermission`, widening booking visibility across organizations; (2) the `isCurrentUser` relaxation lets a caller include themselves in `userIds` to bypass the FORBIDDEN check and read other users' bookings. Tests do not exercise either path, so they pass despite the defects.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `getBookings` in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/get.handler.ts` built its visibility scope by querying `Membership` rows where the caller was ADMIN/OWNER, optionally limited to `user.orgId` and its child teams. It then derived event type, user, and attendee-email sets from those memberships and unioned several Kysely booking queries. PBAC custom roles were ignored on this path.

The PR replaces that membership lookup with `PermissionCheckService.getTeamIdsWithPermission({ permission: 'booking.read', fallbackRoles: [ADMIN, OWNER], orgId })`. That service delegates to `PermissionRepository`, which now runs two raw SQL branches in parallel: one for PBAC custom roles and one for legacy fallback roles on teams without the PBAC feature flag. Both branches are meant to be scoped to the org and its children through a new optional `orgId`. The handler then uses the returned team IDs for event type, member-user, and member-email lookups, so the same scope drives every booking query.
steps: Entry point: the tRPC `bookings.get` procedure calls `getBookings`, which receives the caller (`user` with `orgId`), the filters, and the `kysely` and `prisma` clients.

Scope resolution has changed: `getBookings` calls `PermissionCheckService.getTeamIdsWithPermission` with `booking.read` and the ADMIN/OWNER fallback roles, and passes `orgId: user.orgId ?? undefined`.

The service validates the permission string and forwards to `PermissionRepository`. The single-permission method accepts `orgId` but does not forward it, so scoping is lost at this step (the critical finding).

`PermissionRepository.getTeamIdsWithPermissions` runs `getTeamsWithPBACPermissions` and `getTeamsWithFallbackRoles` in parallel. Each adds `orgId` predicates on Team id and parentId, then the results are unioned.

Back in the handler, the team IDs feed three lookups: event types by team (including managed children via parent), members via `getUserIdsAndEmailsFromTeamIds`, and the `isCurrentUser` guard for the `userIds` filter. The guard is where the authorization regression sits.
The downstream Kysely booking unions are unchanged in shape. Their scope now depends entirely on the team list, so any over-broad team list widens every branch.

findings.title: Authorization bypass: self-inclusion skips the FORBIDDEN check on `userIds`
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/get.handler.ts` (`getBookings`, around lines 145-159), the `isCurrentUser` check was changed from `filters.userIds.length === 1 && user.id === filters.userIds[0]` to `filters.userIds.includes(user.id)`. That lets a caller add their own id to a list of other users and skip the FORBIDDEN guard, which exposes other users' bookings through the `Booking.userId IN` and attendee-email queries. Change the guard so each id in `filters.userIds` must be either the caller or in `allAccessibleUserIds`, and remove the `isCurrentUser` short-circuit. Add a unit test that sends `[self, outsider]` and expects FORBIDDEN.

findings.title: `orgId` is dropped in the single-permission repository path, widening scope across orgs
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/pbac/infrastructure/repositories/PermissionRepository.ts`, `getTeamIdsWithPermission` (around lines 211-223) accepts `orgId` but calls `this.getTeamIdsWithPermissions({ userId, permission, fallbackRoles })` without it, so organization scoping is silently lost. Pass `orgId` through, matching how the plural method forwards it. Add an integration test in `PermissionRepository.integration-test.ts` that calls the singular `getTeamIdsWithPermission` with `orgId` set and asserts teams from other orgs are excluded.

findings.title: `undefined` passed into `$queryRaw` tagged templates when no org is set
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/pbac/infrastructure/repositories/PermissionRepository.ts`, `getTeamIdsWithPermissions` (around lines 246-251) passes a possibly `undefined` `orgId` into the `$queryRaw` tagged templates in `getTeamsWithPBACPermissions` and `getTeamsWithFallbackRoles`. Normalize it to `null` (`orgId ?? null`) before those calls so the SQL null check is explicit and the behavior doesn't depend on how Prisma serializes `undefined`. Also verify that `PermissionCheckService` error swallowing doesn't hide a query failure here, and add a test that calls the method with no `orgId` and asserts a non-empty result.

findings.title: Assertions that cannot fail in the orgId-without-own-user tests
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/get.handler.test.ts`, the `getBookings - PBAC Permission Checks` tests at about lines 249-277, 280-299, and 302-333 end with `.resolves.not.toThrow()`, which doesn't verify anything about the result. Replace each with an assertion on the returned bookings or on the query that reached `kysely`. Add a test where `filters.userIds` is `[user.id, outsiderId]` and assert it throws FORBIDDEN, so the self-inclusion bypass is covered.

findings.title: Tests never exercise `orgId` forwarding from the handler
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/get.handler.test.ts`, add a `getBookings` test with `user.orgId` set to a non-null value, such as 7. Assert that `mockGetTeamIdsWithPermission` is called with `orgId: 7`, which checks that `get.handler.ts` forwards the org scope. The existing test only uses `orgId: null`, so it can't detect a dropped org scope.

findings.title: Unused `TRPCError` import added to the permission service
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/pbac/services/permission-check.service.ts`, remove the `import { TRPCError } from "@trpc/server";` added at line 6. Nothing in the file uses it, and the surrounding methods handle errors by catching and returning `[]`. Confirm with a grep that no `TRPCError` reference remains, then run the lint check.

findings.title: Fallback SQL has a redundant and inconsistent scope predicate
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/pbac/infrastructure/repositories/PermissionRepository.ts`, the org-scope predicates differ between `getTeamsWithPBACPermissions` (child branch, around line 309) and `getTeamsWithFallbackRoles` (child branch, line 357). The fallback version adds `child.parentId = orgId`, which is redundant given the `child.parentId = org.id` join. Make both branches use the same predicate shape, and add a short comment on the intended rule for child teams.

findings.title: Managed child event types are still covered by the team-scoped lookup
findings.body:
The old `getEventTypeIdsWhereUserIsAdminOrOwner` returned event types from both direct teams and parent event types whose team the caller administers. The new path routes through `getEventTypeIdsFromTeamIdsFilter`, which does the same thing: it matches `teamId IN teamIds` and also `parent.teamId IN teamIds`. Managed-event children in sub-teams keep their visibility, so this refactor doesn't regress that case.
